raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes two K-EXAONE-236B-A23B (K-EXAONE 1.0) problems introduced with #50524 (K-EXAONE 2.0 support, 2026-08-03):

1. Checkpoints whose `config.json` predates that change fail to load.
2. With the current official config, the MTP drafter runs its attention without RoPE, which lowers MTP acceptance by 3–5 pp.

## Claims

- **Legacy configs load again.**
  - `"architectures": ["ExaoneMoEForCausalLM"]` resolves through a registry alias, in the same way as `LLaMAForCausalLM`.
  - When `sliding_windows`, `mtp_layer_types` and `mtp_sliding_windows` are missing, `ExaoneMoeAttention` falls back to the scalar `sliding_window`. The MTP layer then takes the settings of the main layer with the same index, which is what vLLM did before #50524.
- **The MTP layer always applies RoPE.** Main-model full-attention layers stay NoPE.
  - With the current official 1.0 config, MTP acceptance goes from 85.0% to 88.3% on GSM8K and from 67.9% to 73.1% on MT-Bench.
  - K-EXAONE 2.0 and legacy 1.0 configs already ran their MTP layer with RoPE (sliding window), so they are unchanged.
- Main-model layers are unchanged for every config. Output quality is unaffected, since spec decoding is lossless.

## Validation

**Setup.** 16× A100-SXM4-40GB. Model: K-EXAONE-236B-A23B FP8 (compressed-tensors), TP=8. Flags: `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, temperature 0, no prefix caching. Two config variants of the same weights: the current official HF config, and a legacy copy predating 2026-08-03.

**Metric.** MTP acceptance comes from the `vllm:spec_decode_num_{draft,accepted}_tokens` counters. Prompts: 200 GSM8K test questions and the 80 MT-Bench prompts. Reruns of the same configuration varied by ≤0.2 pp.

**Loading, `main` @ b2863c0de9**

| checkpoint config | result |
|---|---|
| legacy | `ValidationError: Model architectures ['ExaoneMoEForCausalLM'] are not supported for now` |
| legacy + `--hf-overrides '{"architectures":["ExaoneMoeForCausalLM"]}'` | `AttributeError: 'ExaoneMoeConfig' object has no attribute 'sliding_windows'` |

**MTP acceptance and output throughput** (concurrency 16)

| checkpoint config | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| official, GSM8K | 85.01% (1062 tok/s) | **88.28%** (1081 tok/s) |
| official, MT-Bench | 67.86% (940 tok/s) | **73.07%** (970 tok/s) |
| legacy, GSM8K | fails to load | 88.84% |
| legacy, MT-Bench | fails to load | 74.69% |

GSM8K answer accuracy stays within noise for every run.

**Static check.** I evaluated the old and new logic on every main layer and on the MTP layer, for three configs: legacy 1.0, current 1.0, and K-EXAONE-2.0-750B-A37B.
- Window and RoPE choices for all main layers are identical in every config.
- The only change for configs that load today is the current 1.0 MTP layer, which goes from full + NoPE to full + RoPE.
- K-EXAONE 2.0 is unchanged.

**Tests** (`main` + this PR, A100, TP 8)

```text
pytest tests/models/test_registry.py tests/models/test_initialization.py -k "ExaoneMoE or ExaoneMoe or coverage"
PASSED test_registry_imports[ExaoneMoEForCausalLM]                # new
PASSED test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoEForCausalLM]     # new
PASSED test_registry_imports[ExaoneMoeForCausalLM]
PASSED test_registry_imports[ExaoneMoeMTP]
PASSED test_hf_registry_coverage
PASSED test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoeForCausalLM]
PASSED test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoeMTP]
```

- **Alias coverage.** Removing the alias makes `test_can_initialize_large_subset[ExaoneMoEForCausalLM]` fail with `Model architectures ['ExaoneMoEForCausalLM'] are not supported`.
- **Not covered in CI.** The legacy-field fallback is validated by the end-to-end runs above only. The public repo now serves the new config, so CI cannot load a legacy one.
- **EXAONE 4.5.** `Exaone4_5_ForConditionalGeneration` and `Exaone4_5_MTP` initialization tests also pass. Their MTP layer uses `Exaone4DecoderLayer`, so this PR does not affect them.
- **Lint.** `pre-commit` passes, including mypy-3.12 at the manual stage.

## Details

**Root cause: loading.** #50524 renamed the registry key `ExaoneMoEForCausalLM` to `ExaoneMoeForCausalLM` without keeping an alias. It also replaced `Exaone4Attention`, which reads the scalar `sliding_window`, with code that reads `sliding_windows`, `mtp_layer_types` and `mtp_sliding_windows` directly.

`transformers`' `ExaoneMoeConfig` does not define these fields. The official HF repo added them on the same day ([61e6d57](https://huggingface.co/LGAI-EXAONE/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B/commit/61e6d578eb102b578e5704e2916ac841df9eca0a)), but existing copies kept the old config. Public examples still on it include:
- `furiosa-ai/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-NVFP4A16`
- `Hyun9junn/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-W4A16-G128`
- `haanjack/K-EXAONE-236B-A23B-MXFP4`
- `tazza26/K-EXAONE-236B-SFT-full`

**Root cause: MTP RoPE.** `ExaoneMoeAttention` applied RoPE only to sliding layers. That matches the main model, whose global layers are NoPE in both HF and vLLM. vLLM applied the same rule to the MTP layer, which `transformers` does not implement at all.

- Before #50524, the 1.0 MTP layer inherited layer 0's settings (sliding 128), so it ran with RoPE.
- After #50524 it reads `mtp_layer_types: ["full_attention"]` from the new config, and so loses RoPE.

Measured on v0.30.0, with only the MTP layer's attention changed:

| MTP layer attention | GSM8K | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|
| full, NoPE (current) | 85.05% | 68.32% |
| full, RoPE (this PR) | 88.24% | 73.61% |
| sliding 128, RoPE (pre-#50524) | 88.96% | 74.63% |

RoPE accounts for most of the gap, so the MTP layer was trained with RoPE. This PR keeps the configured attention type and only fixes the positional encoding.

**Duplicate check.** No open issue or PR covers this.
- #50865 (closed) only renamed the test registry key after the HF change.
- #51558 (K-EXAONE-2.0 DSpark) edits `exaone_moe.py` class bases and Eagle hooks, not the attention init.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

AI assistance was used while preparing this PR; I reviewed every changed line and ran all of the validation above myself.

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

-

-                self.sliding_window_size = None
 
-        # apply rotary embeddings to every layer in full attention models
-        self.apply_rope_all_layers = "sliding_attention" not in config.layer_types
+        if layer_types[layer_idx] == "full_attention":
+            self.sliding_window_size = None

+            self.sliding_window_size = sliding_windows[layer_idx]
